verses.text: These are the words Moses spoke to all Israel on the east side of the Jordan River, in the desert, in the Jordan Valley across from Suph, between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Dizahab.
It takes eleven days to travel from Mount Sinai to Kadesh Barnea by the road through the hill country of Seir.
On the first day of the eleventh month, in the fortieth year, Moses told the people of Israel everything the LORD had commanded him to tell them.
This was after he had defeated Sihon, king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, and Og, king of Bashan, who ruled in Ashtaroth and Edrei.
There, east of the Jordan in the land of Moab, Moses began to explain God's teaching. He said:
"When we were at Mount Sinai, the LORD our God said to us, 'You have stayed long enough at this mountain.

Break camp and move on. Go into the hill country of the Amorites and to all the places around it: the Jordan Valley, the hill country, the western foothills, the Negev in the south, and the coast. Go into the land of the Canaanites and to Lebanon, as far as the great Euphrates River.
Look, I have given you this land. Go in and take the land the LORD promised to give to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and to their descendants after them.'"
At that time I said to you, "I cannot carry the load of leading you all by myself.
The LORD your God has made you grow in number, and today you are as many as the stars in the sky.
May the LORD, the God of your ancestors, make you a thousand times more, and bless you as he promised!
But how can I carry all your problems, your burdens, and your arguments by myself?
Choose some wise men with understanding, who are respected in your tribes, and I will make them your leaders."
You answered me, "What you have said is a good idea."

So I took the leaders of your tribes, wise and respected men, and made them your leaders. They were put in charge of groups of a thousand, a hundred, fifty, and ten, and served as officials for your tribes.
At that time I commanded your judges: "Listen to the cases between your people and judge fairly, whether the case is between two Israelites or between an Israelite and a foreigner living among you.

When you judge, do not take sides. Listen to the small and the great alike. Do not be afraid of anyone, because the judgment belongs to God. Bring me any case that is too hard for you, and I will hear it."
At that time I told you everything you should do.
Then, as the LORD our God commanded us, we left Mount Sinai and went through that huge and terrible desert you saw, along the road to the hill country of the Amorites, and we came to Kadesh Barnea.
I said to you, "You have reached the hill country of the Amorites, which the LORD our God is giving us.
Look, the LORD your God has given you the land. Go up and take it, as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, told you. Do not be afraid or lose heart."
Then all of you came to me and said, "Let's send men ahead of us to explore the land for us. They can tell us which road to take and which towns we will come to."
The idea seemed good to me, so I chose twelve of your men, one from each tribe.
They went up into the hill country, came to the Valley of Eshcol, and explored it.
They took some of the fruit of the land and brought it down to us. They reported, "The land the LORD our God is giving us is a good land."
But you refused to go up. You rebelled against the command of the LORD your God.
You complained in your tents and said, "The LORD must hate us. He brought us out of Egypt just to hand us over to the Amorites to destroy us.

Where can we go? Our brothers have made us lose heart. They say, 'The people there are stronger and taller than we are. Their towns are large, with walls up to the sky. We even saw the Anakim there, the giants!'"
Then I said to you, "Do not be terrified or afraid of them.
The LORD your God is going ahead of you, and he will fight for you, just as you saw him do for you in Egypt.
And in the desert you saw how the LORD your God carried you, as a father carries his son, all the way until you reached this place."
But even after this, you did not trust the LORD your God,
who went ahead of you on your journey to find places for you to camp. He showed you the way to go with fire by night and a cloud by day.
When the LORD heard what you said, he was angry and made this solemn promise:
"Not one of the people of this evil generation will see the good land I promised to give your ancestors,
except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He will see it. I will give him and his descendants the land he walked on, because he followed the LORD with all his heart."
Because of you, the LORD was angry with me too, and he said, "You will not enter the land either.
But your helper, Joshua son of Nun, will enter it. Encourage him, because he will lead Israel to take the land as their own.
And your little children, the ones you said would be taken captive, who are too young to know right from wrong, will enter the land. I will give it to them, and they will own it.
But as for you, turn around and go back into the desert, along the road to the Red Sea."

Then you said to me, "We have sinned against the LORD. We will go up and fight, just as the LORD our God commanded us." So every one of you put on his weapons, thinking it would be easy to go up into the hill country.
But the LORD said to me, "Tell them, 'Do not go up and fight, because I will not be with you. Your enemies will defeat you.'"
So I told you, but you would not listen. You rebelled against the LORD's command and proudly marched up into the hill country.
The Amorites who lived in those hills came out against you. They chased you like a swarm of bees and beat you down from Seir all the way to Hormah.
You came back and wept before the LORD, but he would not listen to you or pay attention to you.
So you stayed at Kadesh for a long time, all the time that you stayed there.
